**Module Responsibilities:**

Ledger: Maintains mutable order state (reserved, captured, refunded amounts per order_id) and event deduplication. Outbox: Maintains a queue of {key, payload, version, completed, lease_expiry} items with version-based ownership. enqueue(key, payload) refuses duplicate keys (returns False if equal payload, raises ValueError if different). claim(worker, now, lease) finds the earliest uncompleted item with expired/absent lease, increments version, sets lease_expiry=now+lease, returns {key, payload, version} or None. complete(key, worker, version, now) requires exact owner (worker), exact version, unexpired lease, and not yet completed; returns True/False without side effects on mismatch.

Service: Orchestrates both via ingest() and dispatch(). ingest(event) applies event to ledger, then enqueues notification with key=event['id'] and payload=event. On enqueue failure after ledger apply, rollback ledger to pre-apply state and re-raise. dispatch(worker, now, lease, sink) claims one outbox item, calls sink(key, payload), then attempts complete() with same worker/version at supplied now. **Invariants & Crash Recovery:**
Ledger applies are all-or-nothing; outbox enqueues are independent. Atomicity boundary is in-memory only (snapshot must be persisted separately for true recovery). If ingest dies after enqueue, the notification persists in outbox; on restart, an expired lease allows reclaim and retry, calling sink again. Sink must tolerate re-delivery by keying on event['id']. All three modules snapshot and restore via deep copy (JSON-round-trip safe). Snapshot state includes version counters, lease expiry times, and completion flags; restoration recreates exact state without re-applying events."
